- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep decline, reduce the following 3–5 periods’ forecast by 5–10% to correct for overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean over 5+ periods, apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% per period.  
- If sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.73, 0.86) and forecast is lagging behind recent highs, adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to align with sentiment momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is > 10% above true mean for 3+ consecutive days, apply a mean-reversion correction to bring forecast closer to 30-day moving average.
